sectorImpacts.reason: Falling crude prices generally reduce profitability for upstream oil and gas companies, though refining margins could improve.
Lower crude oil prices directly reduce fuel costs, significantly improving airline profitability.
Reduced fuel costs can boost consumer spending and demand for vehicles, especially in the commercial segment.
Many chemical companies use crude derivatives as feedstock; lower prices can reduce input costs and improve margins.
Lower transportation costs and potentially higher disposable income due to reduced fuel expenses can benefit FMCG demand.
